natural: dressed like a person, acting like a dog

meaning.en: Putting on a respectable, smart look while being no good underneath.
meaning.zh: 装出体面的样子，实际品行不好。

equivalents: all dressed up but a rotter

examples.zh: 他穿上西装，人模狗样的，其实一肚子坏水。
examples.en: In his suit he looks the part, but he's rotten inside.

examples.zh: 别看他人模狗样，做事一点不靠谱。
examples.en: Don't be fooled by his smart look; he's utterly unreliable.

examples.zh: 这帮人模狗样的家伙，背地里干尽了坏事。
examples.en: Those smooth-looking fellows have done every bad thing behind the scenes.

usage.en: Colloquial and rude; 模 is read mú here. Often sarcastic about someone who looks respectable. Attributive or predicate.
usage.zh: 口语，较粗俗；“模”读mú。常讽刺人表面体面。可作定语、谓语。

natural: quick-witted and fond of learning

meaning.en: Clever and keen to learn.
meaning.zh: 聪明而又喜欢学习。

examples.zh: 这孩子敏而好学，老师都很喜欢他。
examples.en: The child is bright and eager to learn, and his teachers all like him.

examples.zh: 她敏而好学，不到三年就精通了三门外语。
examples.en: Quick and studious, she mastered three foreign languages in under three years.

examples.zh: 敏而好学，不耻下问，这是治学的态度。
examples.en: To be quick and keen to learn and not ashamed to ask those below you is the way to study.

story.en: Zigong asked why Kong Wenzi was given the title 'Wen' (cultured). Confucius said: 'He was quick and loved learning, and was not ashamed to ask his inferiors' (敏而好学，不耻下问).
story.zh: 子贡问孔文子为何谥为“文”。孔子说：“敏而好学，不耻下问，是以谓之‘文’也。”

usage.en: Praise, usually of the young; often joined with 不耻下问. Predicate or attributive.
usage.zh: 夸奖，多用于年轻人；常与“不耻下问”连用。可作谓语、定语。

natural: cannot plan together

meaning.en: People with different aims or principles cannot work together.
meaning.zh: 志向、主张不同，不能共同商量或合作。

examples.zh: 道不同，不相为谋，我们还是分开吧。
examples.en: Those on different paths cannot plan together, so let's part ways.

examples.zh: 他们的理念截然相反，不相为谋。
examples.en: Their philosophies are opposite, so they can't cooperate.

examples.zh: 话不投机，两人不相为谋，各自走开了。
examples.en: Finding no common ground, the two went their own ways.

story.en: Confucius said: 'Those whose ways differ cannot make plans together' (道不同，不相为谋).
story.zh: 孔子说：“道不同，不相为谋。”

usage.en: Usually in the saying 道不同，不相为谋. Polite but firm; suggests irreconcilable difference without personal hatred.
usage.zh: 多用于“道不同，不相为谋”。语气委婉而坚决，强调志向不合，不一定有私怨。

natural: lose lustre by comparison

meaning.en: To look dull or inferior when set beside something better.
meaning.zh: 互相比较之下，一方显得逊色。

examples.zh: 和新款相比，旧手机相形失色。
examples.en: Next to the new model, the old phone pales.

examples.zh: 她的舞姿太出众，其他人都相形失色。
examples.en: Her dancing was so outstanding that everyone else was outshone.

examples.zh: 在这座摩天大楼面前，周围的建筑相形失色。
examples.en: Beside this skyscraper the neighbouring buildings look dull.

usage.en: Describes the weaker side; the object of comparison is introduced with 与/在…面前. Predicate.
usage.zh: 形容较弱的一方；比较对象常用“与”“在……面前”引出。作谓语。

natural: sworn brotherhood, strong as gold, fragrant as orchids

meaning.en: To become sworn brothers (or sisters) in a close, loyal bond.
meaning.zh: 结拜为异姓兄弟姐妹，情谊深厚。

examples.zh: 刘备、关羽、张飞桃园三结义，义结金兰。
examples.en: Liu Bei, Guan Yu and Zhang Fei swore brotherhood in the Peach Garden.

examples.zh: 两家姑娘从小要好，长大后义结金兰。
examples.en: The two girls were close since childhood and became sworn sisters as adults.

examples.zh: 他们几个义结金兰，发誓有难同当。
examples.en: The few of them became sworn brothers and vowed to share hardships.

story.en: The Book of Changes: 'When two people are of one heart, their sharpness can cut through metal; words of one heart are as fragrant as orchids' (二人同心，其利断金；同心之言，其臭如兰). 金兰 came to mean sworn friendship.
story.zh: 《周易》：“二人同心，其利断金；同心之言，其臭如兰。”后以“金兰”指结拜之交。

usage.en: Literary; 金兰 means the closest friendship. Fits old-style storytelling and period dramas.
usage.zh: 偏书面语；“金兰”指最亲密的友谊。常见于传统故事和古装剧。

literal: elder brother · friendly · younger brother · respectful
natural: the elder is kind, the younger respectful

meaning.en: Brothers who treat each other well: the elder caring, the younger respectful.
meaning.zh: 兄弟之间相处和睦，哥哥爱护弟弟，弟弟尊敬哥哥。

examples.zh: 他们家兄友弟恭，邻里都称赞。
examples.en: The brothers in that family are so harmonious that the neighbours praise them.

examples.zh: 父母最大的心愿就是儿女兄友弟恭。
examples.en: A parent's greatest wish is for the children to live in fraternal harmony.

examples.zh: 兄友弟恭是传统家风的一部分。
examples.en: Mutual brotherly respect is part of the traditional family ethos.

story.en: The Zuo Zhuan lists the five family virtues: 'the father righteous, the mother kind, the elder brother friendly, the younger brother respectful, the son filial' (父义，母慈，兄友，弟恭，子孝).
story.zh: 《左传》：“父义，母慈，兄友，弟恭，子孝，内平外成。”

usage.en: Formal praise of family harmony; usually about brothers, sometimes extended to siblings. Predicate.
usage.zh: 较书面，称赞家庭和睦；主要指兄弟，也可泛指兄弟姐妹。作谓语。

natural: don't show your silver

meaning.en: Do not let others see your wealth, lest you attract thieves.
meaning.zh: 钱财不要让别人看见，以免招来祸害。

equivalents: keep your wealth out of sight

examples.zh: 出门在外要记住财不露白。
examples.en: When travelling, remember not to flash your cash.

examples.zh: 他把金链子藏进衣服里，说是财不露白。
examples.en: He tucked the gold chain inside his shirt, saying it was best not to show off wealth.

examples.zh: 老人叮嘱孩子，财不露白，免得招贼。
examples.en: The old man warned the child not to show wealth, in case it attracted thieves.

usage.en: A traditional safety saying; 白 stands for silver (白银). A bit old-fashioned but still common.
usage.zh: 传统安全俗语；“白”指白银。略显老式，但仍常用。

natural: regard it as a disgrace

meaning.en: To feel ashamed of something and regard it as a disgrace.
meaning.zh: 把某事当作耻辱。

examples.zh: 他对自己的出身从不引以为耻。
examples.en: He has never been ashamed of his humble origins.

examples.zh: 作弊被发现，他深感引以为耻。
examples.en: Caught cheating, he felt deeply ashamed.

examples.zh: 不懂就问，并不是引以为耻的事。
examples.en: Asking when you don't know is nothing to be ashamed of.

usage.en: Formal; opposite of 引以为荣. Often used with 不 or in the structure 对…引以为耻.
usage.zh: 较书面；与“引以为荣”相对。常用于否定句或“对……引以为耻”。

natural: use the slope to get off the donkey

meaning.en: To seize a convenient chance to back down gracefully and save face.
meaning.zh: 利用台阶、机会摆脱尴尬或下台。

examples.zh: 既然他给了台阶，我就借坡下驴，不再追究了。
examples.en: Since he offered me a way out, I took it and let the matter drop.

examples.zh: 老板一道歉，她就借坡下驴，和好了。
examples.en: As soon as the boss apologised she took the chance to make up.

examples.zh: 他假装没听见，借坡下驴地离开了。
examples.en: He pretended not to hear and slipped away at a convenient moment.

usage.en: Colloquial, northern flavour; can be neutral or slightly sneering at someone using a pretext. Predicate.
usage.zh: 口语，北方色彩；中性，有时略带讥讽，指借机下台。作谓语。

natural: slander piled up melts bones

meaning.en: Constant slander can destroy even a strong person.
meaning.zh: 不断的诽谤足以毁掉一个人。

equivalents: repeated slander wears down the strongest

examples.zh: 积毁销骨，网络暴力让不少人难以承受。
examples.en: Slander piled up can destroy a person, and many cannot bear online abuse.

examples.zh: 众口铄金，积毁销骨，谣言的力量不可小看。
examples.en: Many mouths can melt gold and slander can dissolve bone; never underestimate rumour.

examples.zh: 他一生清白，却被积毁销骨，晚景凄凉。
examples.en: He was blameless all his life but was ruined by accumulated slander and ended up in sorrow.

story.en: Zhang Yi warned the King of Wei: 'Piled-up feathers sink a boat, light loads break an axle, many mouths melt metal, and accumulated slander melts bones' (积羽沉舟，群轻折轴，众口铄金，积毁销骨).
story.zh: 张仪说：“积羽沉舟，群轻折轴，众口铄金，积毁销骨。”

usage.en: Often paired with 众口铄金. A warning about the power of rumour. Predicate or maxim.
usage.zh: 常与“众口铄金”连用，警示谣言的力量。作谓语或格言。

natural: let the spit on one's face dry by itself

meaning.en: To put up with an insult without protest; extreme forbearance, sometimes spinelessness.
meaning.zh: 别人往脸上吐唾沫也不擦，形容忍受侮辱、极度忍让。

examples.zh: 他唾面自干，从不与小人计较。
examples.en: He takes insults on the chin and never quarrels with petty people.

examples.zh: 做人可以大度，但不必唾面自干。
examples.en: One can be magnanimous, but need not meekly swallow insults.

examples.zh: 面对无理的辱骂，她唾面自干，转身走了。
examples.en: Faced with unreasonable abuse she let it pass and walked away.

story.en: Lou Shide told his younger brother that when someone spits in your face you should not wipe it off, lest you anger him; 'let it dry itself' (唾自干耳，当笑而受之).
story.zh: 娄师德教导弟弟，别人唾在脸上不要擦拭，以免激怒对方，“唾自干耳，当笑而受之”。

usage.en: Can be praise (great patience) or criticism (lack of backbone); context decides. Predicate.
usage.zh: 可褒（宽容忍耐）可贬（没有骨气），视语境而定。作谓语。

natural: think of what is right when you see gain

meaning.en: To think first about what is right when faced with a chance of profit.
meaning.zh: 看到有利可图时，先想想是否合乎道义。

examples.zh: 做生意要见利思义，不能坑害顾客。
examples.en: In business you must put principle before profit and not cheat customers.

examples.zh: 他见利思义，拒绝了那笔来路不明的钱。
examples.en: He thought of what was right and turned down the money of dubious origin.

examples.zh: 见利思义，才是君子之风。
examples.en: Weighing righteousness at the sight of profit is the mark of a gentleman.

story.en: Confucius, defining the complete man: 'When he sees gain, he thinks of righteousness; when he sees danger, he gives up his life' (见利思义，见危授命).
story.zh: 孔子论“成人”：“见利思义，见危授命，久要不忘平生之言。”

usage.en: Praise; ethics and honesty. Contrasts with 见利忘义. Predicate.
usage.zh: 褒义；谈品德和诚信。与“见利忘义”相对。作谓语。

natural: the more you look up, the higher it seems

meaning.en: Praise for someone whose learning and character seem ever more lofty the more one studies them.
meaning.zh: 越抬头看越觉得高，赞美人的学问或品德高深。

equivalents: loftier the more you look up

examples.zh: 先生的学问仰之弥高，令后学敬佩。
examples.en: The teacher's learning seems ever more lofty, and later scholars admire him.

examples.zh: 越深入研究，越觉得这位大师仰之弥高。
examples.en: The deeper I study, the more this master seems to tower.

examples.zh: 面对大山，只觉得仰之弥高。
examples.en: Facing the great mountain one can only feel it grows higher the more one looks up.

story.en: Yan Yuan sighed over his teacher: 'The more I look up at it, the higher it is; the more I drill into it, the harder it is' (仰之弥高，钻之弥坚).
story.zh: 颜渊喟然叹曰：“仰之弥高，钻之弥坚。”

usage.en: Very respectful and literary; usually in the pair 仰之弥高，钻之弥坚. Used of teachers or masters.
usage.zh: 十分尊敬，书面语；常与“钻之弥坚”连用。多用于师长、大师。

pinyin: sǐ shēng yǒu mìng, fù guì zài tiān
literal: life · death · has · fate, wealth · rank · rests with · Heaven
natural: life and death are fated, wealth and rank rest with Heaven

meaning.en: Life, death, wealth and status are in the hands of fate; one should accept what cannot be controlled.
meaning.zh: 生死和富贵都由命运决定，人要顺应天命。

examples.zh: 死生有命，富贵在天，不必强求。
examples.en: Life and death are fated, wealth and rank rest with Heaven, so no need to force it.

examples.zh: 他相信富贵在天，对钱财看得很淡。
examples.en: He believes wealth is up to Heaven and takes money lightly.

examples.zh: 别拿富贵在天当借口，不努力是不会成功的。
examples.en: Don't use 'wealth is up to Heaven' as an excuse; without effort you won't succeed.

story.en: Sima Niu lamented that he had no brothers; Zixia consoled him: 'I have heard it said that life and death are decided by fate and wealth and rank by Heaven' (死生有命，富贵在天).
story.zh: 司马牛忧虑自己没有兄弟，子夏说：“商闻之矣：死生有命，富贵在天。”

usage.en: Fatalistic; used to console oneself or to accept things calmly. Can be criticised as passive. Either half may stand alone.
usage.zh: 带宿命论色彩；用来自慰或坦然接受。也可能被批评为消极。上下句可单用。

natural: joyful without excess

meaning.en: Enjoyable but kept within proper bounds; moderate in joy.
meaning.zh: 快乐而有节制，不过度。

examples.zh: 这首诗乐而不淫，哀而不伤。
examples.en: This poem is joyful without excess and sorrowful without grief.

examples.zh: 他喝酒乐而不淫，从不过量。
examples.en: He drinks happily but never to excess.

examples.zh: 过节要乐而不淫，别忘了分寸。
examples.en: Celebrate the holiday cheerfully but with restraint, and keep a sense of proportion.

story.en: Confucius said of the Guanju poem: 'It is joyful but not excessive, sorrowful but not wounding' (《关雎》乐而不淫，哀而不伤).
story.zh: 孔子说：“《关雎》乐而不淫，哀而不伤。”

usage.en: Literary, mostly in arts and manners. 淫 here means 'excessive', not the modern 'lewd'; do not misread it. Often paired with 哀而不伤.
usage.zh: 书面语，多用于文艺与礼仪。这里“淫”指过度，不是现代的“淫秽”之意，勿误解。常与“哀而不伤”连用。

natural: tall as an ox, big as a horse

meaning.en: Big, tall and burly, usually of a person.
meaning.zh: 身材高大魁梧。

examples.zh: 他牛高马大，一个人扛起了两袋米。
examples.en: Built like an ox, he carried two sacks of rice by himself.

examples.zh: 那个牛高马大的保安站在门口。
examples.en: A big burly guard stood at the door.

examples.zh: 别看他牛高马大，其实很胆小。
examples.en: Don't be fooled by his bulk; he's actually timid.

usage.en: Colloquial; often slightly humorous. Mostly for people, sometimes children.
usage.zh: 口语，带幽默意味。多形容人，有时指孩子。

natural: love money as much as life

meaning.en: To be extremely fond of money; miserly.
meaning.zh: 把钱财看得和生命一样重要，非常吝啬贪财。

examples.zh: 他爱财如命，一分钱也不肯多花。
examples.en: He loves money like life itself and won't spend a penny extra.

examples.zh: 那个爱财如命的老板，连员工的奖金都克扣。
examples.en: That miserly boss even docks his staff's bonuses.

examples.zh: 爱钱如命的人，常常失去朋友。
examples.en: People who worship money often lose their friends.

usage.en: Derogatory. Both forms are common; 爱财如命 is slightly more usual.
usage.zh: 贬义。两种说法都常见，“爱财如命”略常用。

literal: Duke of Zhou · spit out · mouthful
natural: the Duke of Zhou spits out his food

meaning.en: A ruler or leader who courteously and eagerly welcomes talented people.
meaning.zh: 指统治者礼贤下士、求才若渴。

equivalents: a leader who courts worthy men

examples.zh: 公司求贤若渴，颇有周公吐哺之风。
examples.en: The company is as eager for talent as the Duke of Zhou was, in his famous example.

examples.zh: 他有周公吐哺的气度，对人才极为礼遇。
examples.en: He has the Duke of Zhou's bearing and treats talent with great courtesy.

examples.zh: 周公吐哺，天下归心。
examples.en: When the Duke of Zhou spat out his food, hearts across the land turned to him.

story.en: The Duke of Zhou said that he once washed his hair and three times grabbed it up, and ate a meal and three times spat out his food, to receive visitors (一沐三捉发，一饭三吐哺).
story.zh: 周公自述：“一沐三捉发，一饭三吐哺，起以待士，犹恐失天下之贤人。”

usage.en: Praise for leaders; often with 天下归心. Allusion to Duke of Zhou, regent of the early Zhou dynasty. Literary.
usage.zh: 夸奖领导者；常与“天下归心”连用。典出周初摄政的周公。书面语。

pinyin: péng shēng má zhōng, bù fú ér zhí
literal: mugwort · grow · hemp · among, not · prop · yet · straight
natural: mugwort growing among hemp stands straight unsupported

meaning.en: A person who grows up in good company becomes upright without being forced.
meaning.zh: 蓬草长在麻中，不用扶持也长得挺直，比喻良好环境能使人向善。

equivalents: a good environment straightens the crooked

examples.zh: 蓬生麻中，不扶而直，选好朋友对孩子很重要。
examples.en: Mugwort among hemp grows straight; choosing good friends is vital for children.

examples.zh: 他在书香门第长大，真是蓬生麻中，不扶而直。
examples.en: He grew up in a scholarly family and, like mugwort among hemp, grew up straight.

examples.zh: 环境的影响如蓬生麻中，潜移默化。
examples.en: The influence of surroundings is like mugwort in hemp, working unnoticed.

story.en: Xunzi: 'Mugwort growing among hemp stands up straight without support; white sand in black mud turns black with it' (蓬生麻中，不扶而直；白沙在涅，与之俱黑).
story.zh: 荀子：“蓬生麻中，不扶而直；白沙在涅，与之俱黑。”

usage.en: Positive side of environmental influence; its pair is 白沙在涅，与之俱黑 (white sand in black mud turns black). Often shortened to 蓬生麻中.
usage.zh: 强调环境的积极影响；与“白沙在涅，与之俱黑”相对。常简称“蓬生麻中”。

antonyms: 染于苍则苍，染于黄则黄

natural: a brat makes a name

meaning.en: A worthless youngster gets famous for lack of better men; used sarcastically of unworthy people who rise to fame.
meaning.zh: 无能之辈成了名，多用来讽刺不配成名的人。

examples.zh: 时无英雄，遂使竖子成名。
examples.en: With no heroes about, upstarts get to make a name.

examples.zh: 这种作品也能获奖，真是竖子成名。
examples.en: For a work like this to win a prize is truly an upstart making a name.

examples.zh: 他对网红走红不屑，感叹竖子成名。
examples.en: He scorned the rise of influencers and sighed that mere boys were becoming famous.

story.en: Ruan Ji once climbed Guangwu Mountain, looked at the old battlefield of Chu and Han and sighed: 'When there were no heroes, it let a brat make a name' (时无英雄，使竖子成名).
story.zh: 阮籍登广武山，观楚汉战场，叹道：“时无英雄，使竖子成名！”

usage.en: Sarcastic, haughty and literary; 竖子 means 'brat', a contemptuous term. Avoid being too serious or applying it to real people.
usage.zh: 讽刺，带傲慢，书面语；“竖子”是轻蔑称呼。注意不要对真人用得太认真。

literal: fragrant zhi herb · orchid · of · room
natural: a room of irises and orchids

meaning.en: A fine environment, or the company of good people, which gradually refines one's character.
meaning.zh: 比喻良好的环境或贤人的交往，使人受益。

examples.zh: 与善人居，如入芝兰之室，久而不闻其香。
examples.en: To live with good people is to enter a room of orchids: after a while you no longer smell the fragrance.

examples.zh: 这所学校就像芝兰之室，熏陶了一代代学子。
examples.en: The school is like a room of orchids that has nurtured generations of students.

examples.zh: 他有幸在芝兰之室中长大，气质不凡。
examples.en: He was lucky to grow up in such a refined setting and has a fine bearing.

story.en: Confucius: 'Living with good people is like entering a room of irises and orchids: after a time you no longer smell the scent, because you have become one with it' (与善人居，如入芝兰之室，久而不闻其香).
story.zh: 孔子说：“与善人居，如入芝兰之室，久而不闻其香，即与之化矣。”

usage.en: Literary praise of environment or company. Often paired with 鲍鱼之肆 (the fish market) as contrast.
usage.zh: 书面语，赞美环境或交往对象。常与“鲍鱼之肆”对举。

natural: thirty-six trades

meaning.en: All kinds of trades and occupations (the number is traditional, not literal).
meaning.zh: 泛指各种行业。

examples.zh: 三十六行，行行出状元。
examples.en: Of the thirty-six trades, every one produces a champion.

examples.zh: 他干过三十六行，什么活都懂一点。
examples.en: He has worked in every trade and knows a bit of everything.

examples.zh: 社会有三十六行，职业无贵贱。
examples.en: Society has thirty-six trades and no occupation is higher or lower.

usage.en: Neutral; 行 is read háng ('trade'). The set saying is 三十六行，行行出状元. Also seen as 七十二行.
usage.zh: 中性；“行”读háng（行业）。常说“三十六行，行行出状元”。也有“七十二行”之说。

natural: face flushing red then white in anger

meaning.en: Flustered and angry, red-faced and pale with agitation.
meaning.zh: 形容着急、发火时脸色红白不定的样子。

examples.zh: 有话好好说，别急赤白脸的。
examples.en: Say what you have to say calmly; don't get so worked up.

examples.zh: 他急赤白脸地跟人争了起来。
examples.en: He started arguing with someone in a flushed, agitated state.

examples.zh: 为这点小事急赤白脸，不值得。
examples.en: It's not worth getting hot under the collar over such a trifle.

usage.en: Colloquial, mostly northern; also written 急头白脸. Adverbial or predicate.
usage.zh: 口语，多见于北方；也作“急头白脸”。作状语或谓语。

natural: a gentleman holds firm in poverty

meaning.en: A man of integrity stays upright even in poverty and hardship.
meaning.zh: 君子在穷困中仍能坚守节操。

equivalents: a gentleman holds firm in hardship

examples.zh: 君子固穷，他宁可饿肚子也不收贿赂。
examples.en: A gentleman stays firm in poverty; he would rather go hungry than take a bribe.

examples.zh: 她安贫乐道，君子固穷，从不抱怨。
examples.en: Content with poverty and true to principle, she never complains.

examples.zh: 君子固穷，小人穷斯滥矣，这是孔子的话。
examples.en: 'The gentleman holds firm in poverty; the petty man in poverty runs wild': those are Confucius's words.

story.en: Stranded without food in Chen, Zilu asked angrily if a gentleman could also be poor. Confucius answered: 'A gentleman is certainly poor at times, but a petty man in poverty runs wild' (君子固穷，小人穷斯滥矣).
story.zh: 孔子在陈绝粮，子路愠见曰：“君子亦有穷乎？”子曰：“君子固穷，小人穷斯滥矣。”

usage.en: Praise of integrity. Original line contrasts it with 小人穷斯滥矣 (the petty man turns reckless when poor). Predicate or maxim.
usage.zh: 赞扬气节。原句后接“小人穷斯滥矣”（小人穷困就胡作非为）。作谓语或格言。

synonyms: 富贵不能淫，贫贱不能移，威武不能屈
